title: Audit: which backend-computed data has no UI consumer at all
description:
User-requested audit: find backend-provided functionality (an endpoint, or a response-schema field within an endpoint already called by the frontend) that currently has NO consumer anywhere in a production UI component. This is scoped specifically to 'does the UI ever render/use this value', not 'does the signal/confidence engine use this value internally' -- docs/Analyse.md uses similar-sounding language ('detection + exposure only', 'not wired into signal/confidence') for a different, already-understood, already-intentional gap (backend-internal, about `app.signals`/`app.portfolio` wiring, not about the UI) -- don't conflate the two. Two concrete examples already confirmed by reading the current code before writing this task, to calibrate what counts:

- `RiskPosition.trailing_stop` (`GET /api/portfolio/risk`, backend/app/portfolio/risk.py's `ratchet_trailing_profit_stop`): typed in `frontend/src/api/types.ts`, but grep confirms no production component reads `trailing_stop`/`trailingStop` anywhere -- `PositionsTable.tsx`'s 'Protective Stop' column and `HeldPositionBanner.tsx`'s 'Current Stop' field both show only the raw, un-ratcheted `protective_stop`. **Already filed as its own task, `frontend-trailing-stop-display` -- don't re-file this one.**
- `GET /api/cftc/cot`: confirmed via grep that there is no `frontend/src/api/cftc.ts` (or any file) calling this endpoint at all -- zero frontend consumption of any kind, not even a schema-field-level gap within an otherwise-used response. Check whether this is deliberate backend-only infrastructure (e.g. feeding some other internal computation, not meant for direct UI display) before assuming it's a pure UI gap -- read `docs/tasks/done/backend-cftc-cot-data*.json`'s own decisions for why it was built, and grep the backend for any internal caller of `app.data.cftc_cot_provider`/the CFTC endpoint's underlying data beyond the router itself.

A third candidate worth checking carefully rather than assuming either way: `AnalysisResponse.divergence.aborted` (the 'Hound of the Baskervilles' flag) is typed and present in test fixtures (`PriceChart.test.tsx`/`OscillatorChart.test.tsx`/`StockCharts.test.tsx`), but grep confirms no production chart code reads it. docs/Analyse.md §5 item 5 says 'Exposed as `aborted` -- detected and exposed only; this app doesn't (yet) act on it,' which reads ambiguously as to whether that's about signal-wiring (the usual sense of that phrase in this doc) or also covers 'not shown in the UI either' as an accepted, already-decided gap -- don't silently exclude it either way; read the referenced task's own decisions, and record your own judgment call explicitly.

`backend-ibkr-import-entry-date-from-trades` (sibling task in this same batch, IBKR import's `entry_date` always being today's date) is a related but distinct kind of gap -- not 'unused backend data' but 'backend data that's genuinely unavailable/not yet fetched at all' -- also already tracked, don't re-file.

checklist.step: Enumerate every backend API endpoint (grep `@router.(get|post|put|patch|delete)` across backend/app/api/routers/*.py) and confirm each one has at least one real caller in frontend/src/api/*.ts (not just a type definition in types.ts). Note any endpoint with zero frontend callers.

For every field on a response schema already fetched by the frontend (backend/app/api/schemas.py's response models for endpoints that DO have a frontend caller), grep frontend/src/features/**/*.tsx and frontend/src/components/**/*.tsx (excluding *.test.tsx, api/types.ts, and the api client wrapper files themselves) for an actual read of that field name. Compile the list of fields with zero production-component usage.

For each endpoint/field found above, determine whether it's (a) a deliberate, already-documented 'not surfaced in UI' decision not worth re-raising (read the referenced task's own `decisions` entry to confirm, don't assume from the field's docstring alone), (b) already covered by `frontend-trailing-stop-display` or `backend-ibkr-import-entry-date-from-trades` (don't re-file these), or (c) a genuine, previously-untracked UI gap.

File a new tracked follow-up task (state `planned`, its own concrete description/checklist grounded in the actual code read -- not a generic placeholder) for every genuine gap found under (c), add each to docs/tasks/index.json, and run `python3 scripts/validate_tasks.py` to confirm the board is still structurally valid. Implementing a fix directly within THIS task is fine only for a genuinely trivial case (your own judgment call, recorded as a decision) -- the default is to file, not fix, since this task's job is the audit.

Record the full findings list as a `decisions` entry on this task -- including what was checked and deliberately ruled out (not only what became a new task), so a future reader doesn't have to re-derive the same audit from scratch.

decisions.decision: `AnalysisResponse.divergence.aborted` (the 'Hound of the Baskervilles' flag) is judged NOT a UI gap -- it already has a production consumer, via `frontend/src/features/stocks/components/metricHelpContent.ts`'s `divergenceHelp.interpretValue(divergence, inVisibleRange)`, which appends a dedicated 'Hound of the Baskervilles' explanatory clause whenever `aborted` is true. That function is called from production (non-test) code in both `OscillatorChart.tsx` and `PriceChart.tsx`, each passing its result into `MetricHelp`'s `valueInterpretation` prop, which `MetricHelp.tsx` renders inside its info popover (confirmed by reading `MetricHelp.tsx` itself: `{valueInterpretation && (...{valueInterpretation})}`). So the flag is read and does change what the user sees in the UI (the divergence legend's help tooltip text), even though it has no separate visual chart marker of its own (no distinct marker/icon on the chart canvas beyond the tooltip). This task's own description flagged this as genuinely ambiguous and asked for an explicit judgment call: `git log -S"abortedClause"` confirms this tooltip wiring has existed since 2026-09-19 (commit 5018850f, PR #151-era), predating this audit by weeks -- so the task description's calibration note ('grep confirms no production chart code reads it') was itself already stale by the time this audit ran, most likely written before that tooltip wiring landed or based on an incomplete grep that missed the indirect metricHelpContent.ts -> OscillatorChart.tsx/PriceChart.tsx call chain. No follow-up task filed for this field.
decisions.rationale: The bar for 'has a UI consumer' this task sets is 'does the UI ever render/use this value', not 'does it have its own dedicated visual treatment' -- a tooltip/help-text consumer counts, the same way `supportResistanceZoneHelp.interpretValue` reading `zone.broken`/`zone.false_breakout` to build explanatory text (also tooltip-only, no separate chart marker beyond the dashed-border/arrow-marker treatment those two already get) was never in question as a gap. Rejected treating this as a gap purely because the task description suggested it as a candidate -- re-reading the actual current code is what this audit is for, and the code doesn't match the stale premise.

decisions.decision: Full audit findings. Method: (1) enumerated every `@router.(get|post|put|patch|delete)` across backend/app/api/routers/*.py (27 endpoints across cftc/homework/ibkr/portfolio/settings/stocks/watchlist) and matched each against frontend/src/api/*.ts's `request<...>('/api/...')` call sites by literal path -- every endpoint has at least one frontend caller EXCEPT `GET /api/cftc/cot` and `GET /api/daily-homework` (list_daily_homework), both confirmed zero frontend callers of any kind (not even a reference in a hook or component, only in generated frontend/src/api/types.ts). (2) For every response schema field on an endpoint that DOES have a frontend caller, grepped frontend/src/features/**/*.tsx, frontend/src/components/**/*.tsx, and feature-level non-test .ts helper files (metricHelpContent.ts, methodologyContent.ts, exitFlagLabels.ts, totalRiskHelp.ts, marketBreadthHelp.ts) for both the snake_case field name and its camelCase equivalent, excluding *.test.*, api/types.ts, and the api/*.ts client wrapper files themselves. GENUINE GAPS FILED AS NEW TASKS: (a) `frontend-cftc-cot-display` -- GET /api/cftc/cot, confirmed zero frontend consumption of any kind; confirmed (via grep across backend/app for CFTCCOTProvider/CFTCCOTCache callers) it is also not quietly feeding any internal backend computation beyond its own router, so this isn't deliberate backend-only infrastructure either -- it is simply unused end-to-end. (b) `frontend-trade-strategy-tagging` -- PositionIn.strategy/PositionOut.strategy/ClosedTradeOut.strategy: a complete, fully-implemented backend feature (3 done tasks) with literally zero frontend input or display anywhere -- AddPositionDialog.tsx has an entry_notes input but no strategy input; TradeJournalPanel.tsx has a Notes column but no Strategy column; PositionsTable.tsx has neither. The clearest and highest-value gap found, by contrast with entry_notes/follow_up_notes, each of which got its own matching frontend task when built. (c) `frontend-daily-homework-history` -- GET /api/daily-homework (list), confirmed zero frontend caller; DailyHomeworkPage only ever shows today's single entry, with no way to see a trend over time despite the backend endpoint's own docstring describing exactly that use case. ALREADY COVERED, NOT RE-FILED: `RiskPosition.trailing_stop` (frontend-trailing-stop-display, now done -- re-confirmed via `git log` that PR #399 merged shortly before this audit started, and PositionsTable.tsx/HeldPositionBanner.tsx now both read trailing_stop) and IBKR import's always-today entry_date (backend-ibkr-import-entry-date-from-trades, still planned). CHECKED AND DELIBERATELY RULED OUT (real zero-usage fields found, but judged too minor/already-effectively-covered to warrant a dedicated follow-up task): `SupportResistanceZone.dollar_volume`/`touch_count`/`length_days`/`height_pct`/`break_date` -- the zone feature itself is fully built and visualized (role/upper/lower/height_category/length_category/strength_score/broken/false_breakout are all read by PriceChart.tsx/metricHelpContent.ts per frontend-support-resistance-overlay's own explicit design decisions), these are secondary metadata sub-fields of an already-shown concept, not a hidden feature; `IBKRBreadthSnapshotResponse.snapshot_date` -- always equals today's date whenever available per its own schema description, so has negligible display value; `DailyHomeworkOut.recorded_at` -- naturally folds into the frontend-daily-homework-history task filed above rather than needing its own separate task. EVERY OTHER FIELD CHECKED (full list grepped: rsi, season, trend_strength/atr/plus_di/minus_di/adx, obv, accumulation_distribution, insider_clusters, kangaroo_tail, divergence, false_breakout, profit_target/reward_risk_ratio/meets_minimum_reward_risk/distance_to_stop/distance_to_target, buy_grade_pct/sell_grade_pct/trade_grade_pct/trade_letter_grade, exit_flags, weekly_macd_histogram_slope, showed_pullback_in_lookback/showed_rally_in_lookback, earnings_within_warning_days/ex_dividend_date/shares_short/short_ratio/short_percent_of_float/float_shares/insider_transactions, current_price_change_pct, realized_losses_this_month_pct/total_open_risk_pct/six_percent_rule_breached/two_percent_rule_breached/position_risk_pct, entry_notes, equity/positions_value, unavailable_reason, go/total_score, login_url, IBKR scanner categories/rank/company_name/conid, IBKR portfolio-preview/preload conflict fields) was confirmed to have at least one real production (non-test, non-type-only) consumer -- no gap.
decisions.rationale: Scoped strictly to 'does the UI ever render/use this value' per the task's own framing, not 'does the signal/confidence engine use it' (the latter is a separate, already-understood, already-intentional backend-internal gap this task was explicitly told not to conflate with a UI gap -- most 'detection + exposure only'/'not wired into signal/confidence' schema fields in this codebase, e.g. divergence, kangaroo_tail, support_resistance_zones, season, trend_strength, obv/accumulation_distribution, DO have real UI consumers despite that docstring phrasing, confirming the task description's own warning about this exact conflation risk was well-founded). Filed 3 new tasks rather than fixing any of them directly within this audit task, per the task's own default ('implementing a fix directly within THIS task is fine only for a genuinely trivial case') -- none of the three genuine gaps found is trivial: each needs real UI design decisions (placement, input conventions, a MetricHelp entry) that belong in their own task-worker pass with their own tests/Storybook coverage, not squeezed into an audit task's commit.
